messages:
sam_lee: Heads-up: AuroraPay on Dedicated (us-west-2, pool:d-6-gpu) started seeing a flood of 429s ~10:02 PDT. Customer says it kicked off a promo -> lots of long-context generation (20k-40k tokens). Not seeing auth/billing errors. KV eviction rate shot up and autoscaler did not expand quickly.
meera_n: Can you paste the kvcache evict/alloc logs and the pool id? Also model + seq len distribution?
sam_lee: pool:d-6-gpu, model: llama-2-13b-q8, traffic spike around 10:01-10:05. Logs: 
```
[10:02:11] kvcache: entries=1.2M alloc_mb=11200 evict_rate=9.4/s frag_pct=28
[10:02:22] kvcache: evict_burst=1200 window=60s longctx_hits=0.06
[10:03:03] serve: 429 -> route=dedicated-pool throttle=kvcache_pressure
```
tom_garcia: infra-bot posted a capacity alert around 10:04, linking it here. @infra-bot any autoscale events? :eyes:
infra-bot: ALERT: dedicated-pool:d-6-gpu high_kvcache_eviction (10:02:00 - 10:06:00). Autoscaler: scale_up_attempts=1 failed_quota, fallback_policy=graceful-throttle. See runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-pressure
meera_n: Failed_quota — that suggests we hit account-level GPU quota or cloud provider transient. But evict_rate and frag_pct look high. Could be fragmentation + long ctx causing many small allocations. Can someone get jemalloc stats and a heap profile from one of the affected nodes?
iris_ops: I'm grabbing jemalloc stats now, also running `pmap` + `nvml` checks. Quick command to reproduce load locally for repro: 
```bash
# synthetic long-context repro (inc token length 30k - causes many KV slots)
python tools/clients/loadgen.py --host dedicated-usw2 --pool d-6-gpu --concurrency 80 --prompt-file tests/long_promos.txt --max-tokens 30000
```
support-sre: Adding notes to the escalation ticket: tenant=aurorapay, created_incident=INC-2026-214. Temporary mitigation suggestions: 1) enable tenant reservation + cap concurrent longctx per-tenant 2) apply eviction-throttle window to avoid cascade 3) fallback to quantized smaller model for overflow.
sam_lee: Tried a local repro with loadgen above, reproduced eviction burst but autoscaler still didn't add nodes — cloud quota error in the autoscaler logs: `quotaExceeded: requested 2 gpus, available 0`. We should treat this differently: avoid immediate retrying scale that fails and instead apply per-tenant soft-limits.
meera_n: Agree. Also there is clear evidence of memory fragmentation: frag_pct ~28 and evict_burst high. Two-pronged: short-term throttle + reconfigure allocator (larger slab size for kv entries) medium-term. Can we bubble this change as a config for dedicated pools?
tom_garcia: Patch proposal: allow pool-level `kv_slab_size_mb` override and tenant `longctx_concurrency_limit`. I'll draft a PR. Meanwhile, support-sre, please push the mitigation to AuroraPay: cap concurrency to 12 longctx requests and enable eviction-throttle (window: 120s, soft_limit: 8/s).
support-sre: Will do. Communicated to AuroraPay: "Applying temporary concurrency cap + model fallback; engineering investigating memory fragmentation. We'll follow up with timeline." :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: NOTE: autoscaler.log snippet: 
```
[10:03:12] scale_up: attempted=2 requested_gpu=2 result=quotaExceeded provider_msg="Quota limit reached"
[10:03:55] fallback: policy=graceful-throttle applied_to=pool:d-6-gpu
```
iris_ops: Collected jemalloc dumps and heap ASCII map; sending to eng-ml channel for allocator review. Early glance: many small freed regions, high churn. Suggest enabling coalescing and increasing slab bucket size for kv items.
meera_n: Can we also add a temporary route to redirect overflow longctx to hosted-api (ephemeral, cheaper model) while keeping tenant data isolation via token-sanitization? Might reduce burn while we patch. Thoughts @tom_garcia?
tom_garcia: Feasible: route policy `overflow:hosted-llm-quant` with data redaction layer. Need support from product but doable as emergency escape hatch. I'll sketch the config.
sam_lee: Customer visible update posted at 10:35: "We identified cache pressure from long-context workloads causing evictions. We've applied a temporary concurrency cap and fallback to a lower-memory variant to mitigate 429s. Engineering is working on allocator and pool config changes."
support-sre: AuroraPay replied: "Thanks, can you confirm no billing surprises? We'll pause promo if needed." I confirmed no billing anomalies.
meera_n: Next steps: (1) tom - PR for `kv_slab_size_mb` + tenant limit (2) eng-ml/infra - validate allocator coalescing changes in a canary pool (3) product - approve overflow-hosted route (4) support - follow up with customer post-mitigation. I'll schedule a short postmortem.
sam_lee: Thanks all. I'll keep thread updated with canary results. :bow:
